notes:
Summary: evaluation focused on delivering deterministic low-latency completions inside IDE with predictable token spend. Primary ask: TTFT < 60ms for single-line inline completions; acceptable suggestion generation window < 180ms. Must minimize jitter (target stddev < 15ms) to avoid cursor-hopping UX issues.

Key requirements / quotes from CTO (Anita Rao): 
- "We need first-token consistently under 60ms for local file completions — spikes kill the experience."
- Backpressure: client must gracefully degrade when token budget exceeded (partial streaming + token-boundary hints).
- Model/version pinning: want to pin stable release for GA (e.g., 13B quantized variant), but need automated fallback to cheaper model during load.

Functional priorities (short):
- Low TTFT for inline completions (30-60ms target)
- Streaming partial tokens immediately (sub-token flush) for perceived speed
- Token budget policies: 1) inline: max 40 tokens, 2) long suggestion: 200 tokens, 3) configurable per-project defaults
- Jitter control: prioritized warm routing + persistent sessions to re-use KV caches
- Backpressure API: SDK-level signal + server-side preemption to stop generation when budget hits threshold

POC success metrics (agreed):
- Median TTFT (dev machine -> client first byte) < 60ms across 95th percentile of test corpus
- 95th-percentile latency for full suggestions < 220ms when under committed throughput
- Jitter (latency stddev) < 15ms for interactive path
- Token overspend rate < 1.5% vs budget after tuning

Technical Preferences / Notes:
- Prefer VPC Dedicated for predictable throughput; will consider hosted for MVP if latency SLA demonstrable.
- Want instrumentation: token-level latency traces, trace id correlation to editor sessions, per-route cost breakdowns.
- Model ops: must support pinning to exact model checksum, ability to roll back to previous version within 15 minutes.
- Asked about Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching thresholds and quantization profiles tailored to streaming workloads.
